This analysis is the conjunction [Leading>Rest] ∩ [Following>Rest] in leaders-only and primarily identifies sensorimotor/motor networks for movement rather than social-cognitive processing; it does not specifically isolate social processing at the contrast level.
The contrast does not measure affiliation/attachment or bonding-related processes; the analysis indexes general sensorimotor activation, so affiliation/attachment criteria are not met.
The contrast does not isolate communicative signal processing (e.g., speech, gaze, prosody) at the contrast level; it is a general movement conjunction.
The conjunction reflects motor execution/planning common to leading and following rather than an explicit self-referential or agency contrast; PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 is not satisfied.
This analysis does not specifically index representations/inference about others (mental states, intentions) but instead shows shared sensorimotor activations; PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1 is not met.

This is the conjunction [Leading>Rest] ∩ [Following>Rest] in followers-only and mainly reveals sensorimotor network activity rather than specific social-cognitive processing; it does not isolate social processing at the contrast level.
The analysis does not target affiliation or attachment constructs; it reflects general movement-related activations.
No communicative signal exchange (e.g., speech, gaze, prosody) is isolated by this conjunction contrast; it indexes movement-related activity.
The contrast does not explicitly isolate self-referential or agency processing; it identifies general sensorimotor activations common to both roles.
While the task is social, this specific conjunction does not isolate inference/representation about others' mental states or intentions; PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1 is not satisfied.

Whole-group Leading vs Following is a group-level, whole-brain task contrast from healthy adults that contrasts two roles in a joint-action (social) task and reveals social-cognitive networks (e.g., TPJ, PCC for following); the contrast therefore indexes social processing.
The contrast contrasts task roles (leading vs following) and does not specifically measure affiliation, bonding, or attachment constructs at the contrast level.
Although social interaction is present, the contrast does not specifically isolate communicative signal processing (e.g., speech, gaze, prosody or gesture communication) at the contrast level.

Although leading-related areas (e.g., DLPFC, SMA) are interpretable as involving self-initiation/agency, the contrast is not an explicit self-vs-other or dedicated agency manipulation and thus does not meet PERCEPTION_SELF_I1.

The Leading vs Following contrast in the whole group reveals regions associated with understanding others' actions/intentions (e.g., TPJ, PCC, pSTS for following-related activations), thus directly indexing perception/understanding of others.

Leaders-only Leading vs Following primarily highlights motor/planning regions (SMA, PMC, SPL) and shows little evidence of social-cognitive activations; the contrast does not specifically index social processing in this subgroup.
The leaders-only contrast does not measure affiliation/attachment-related constructs.
The contrast isolates role-specific motor/planning activations and does not isolate communicative signal processing.
Although leader-related activations relate to action initiation, the leaders-only contrast is not an explicit self-referential/agency manipulation and thus does not meet PERCEPTION_SELF_I1.
The leaders-only contrast lacks evidence of regions indexing inference/representation about others (mentalizing) and therefore does not meet PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1.
Followers-only Leading vs Following shows follower-specific activations in mentalizing/social regions (PCC, TPJ, pSTS) and therefore indexes social processing in this subgroup.
The contrast isolates follower-related mentalizing/perception but does not specifically target affiliation or attachment constructs.
Although social perception regions are engaged, the analysis does not specifically isolate communicative signal exchange (gaze, prosody, speech, gesture) at the contrast level.
The followers-only contrast emphasizes inference/tracking of others rather than self-referential or agency processes; PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 is not met.
Followers-only contrast reveals activations in regions (TPJ, PCC, pSTS) that index perception and inference about others' actions and intentions, satisfying the perception-of-others criterion.

The regression of Leading>Following with leader skill identifies premotor/motor and insula/STG regions linked to motor control and improvisation; it does not specifically index social-cognitive processing.
This covariation with leader skill does not target affiliation/attachment constructs.
Although STG appears, the analysis does not isolate communicative signal processing (speech/gaze/prosody) at the contrast level; it primarily reflects motor/ improvisation-related covariation.
While leader-skill covariation implicates areas involved in action planning/initiative, the regression is not an explicit self-referential or agency contrast and does not meet PERCEPTION_SELF_I1.
The leader-skill regression highlights motor/premotor systems rather than regions indexing inference about others; PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1 is not satisfied.
The reported deactivation map for leader-skill regression is not described as indexing social processing; no evidence the deactivations isolate social-cognitive processes.
The deactivation analysis does not measure affiliation/attachment constructs.
No evidence that the deactivation contrast isolates communicative signal processing.
The deactivation map is not an explicit self-referential/agency contrast; PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 is not met.
The deactivation analysis does not provide evidence for representation/inference about others and therefore does not meet PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1.
The regression of Leading>Following with follower skill reveals activity in canonical social/mentalizing regions (mPFC, PCC, TPJ, pSTS) during following, which directly indexes social processing.
Although social/mentalizing regions are engaged, the regression specifically indexes follower skill rather than affiliation/bonding constructs; AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 is not met.

The analysis implicates mentalizing and biological-motion regions (pSTS/TPJ) but does not isolate communicative-signal exchange (speech/gaze/prosody) at the contrast level, so SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 is not met.
The follower-skill regression targets perception/mentalizing about others rather than explicit self-referential or agency processing; PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 is not satisfied.
The regression identifies TPJ, pSTS, PCC and mPFC whose activity covaries with follower skill, directly indexing the representation/inference of others' actions and intentions.

Group-level whole-brain contrast (emotional > neutral) during the Empathic Accuracy Task on healthy adults directly indexes social/emotional processing of others' expressions and stories; meets global sample and whole-brain requirements and specifically indexes social processing.
Contrast does not isolate affiliation/attachment or bonding/relationship-related processing at the contrast level.

The contrast contrasts emotional storytelling (speech, prosody, facial expressions) vs neutral storytelling, which implicates receptive processing of communicative signals (speech/prosody/expressions) at the contrast level in a whole-brain group map of healthy adults.
Contrast does not isolate self-referential or agency processing (self vs other) at the contrast level; it focuses on perceiving others' emotional content.

Emotional > neutral contrast in the EAT indexes neural responses to others' emotional states and expressive cues; analysis is a whole-brain group map in healthy adults directly relating to perception/inference about others' emotions.

The neutral > emotional contrast mainly highlights control-dominant / non-emotional activity (e.g., increased mind-wandering/visual-spatial imagery in neutral clips) and does not specifically index social/emotional processing; thus it is excluded under the global control-dominant exclusion.
Contrast does not isolate affiliation/attachment-related processing at the contrast level.
Neutral > emotional contrast does not isolate communicative-signal processing (it reflects higher activation during neutral control clips rather than communication-specific processing).
Contrast does not isolate self-referential processing at the contrast level.

The neutral > emotional contrast does not index perception/inference about others' emotional states (it reflects greater activity during a non-emotional control), so it fails the contrast-level requirement for this construct.

Parametric modulation by intra-individual empathic accuracy (Z-EA) during emotional clips is a whole-brain group-level task-evoked map in healthy adults that indexes variation in social processing (tracking others' emotions).
The modulation by empathic accuracy does not specifically isolate affiliation/attachment or bonding-related processing at the contrast level.

While communicative signals contribute to empathic accuracy, the reported contrast specifically indexes accuracy in inferring others' emotions rather than isolating communication per se; it does not meet the communication-isolation local inclusion criterion.
The modulation by Z-EA targets accuracy in perceiving others, not self-referential or agency processes; it does not isolate self-processing.

Variation in empathic accuracy (Z-EA) directly indexes participants' representation/inference of others' emotional states; the contrast is a whole-brain group map in healthy adults mapping perception/understanding of others.

Negative modulation by intra-individual empathic accuracy is a whole-brain, group-level task-evoked map in healthy adults that pertains to social/empathic processing and thus meets global and local social-processing criteria.
The negative modulation does not isolate affiliation/attachment-related processing at the contrast level.
The contrast indexes variation in empathic accuracy rather than isolating communicative-signal processing, so it does not meet the social communication inclusion criterion.
The contrast measures variation in perceiving others (EA) rather than self-referential processing; it does not isolate perception_self.

Negative modulation by Z-EA still indexes the relation between neural activity and accuracy in representing others' emotional states; it is a whole-brain, within-healthy-group measure of perception/understanding of others.

Time-series correlation between BOLD and participants' continuous ratings of targets' emotional intensity is a whole-brain, task-evoked group map in healthy adults directly indexing social/emotional processing of others.
This contrast indexes moment-to-moment tracking of others' emotional intensity rather than affiliation/bonding/attachment-specific processing.

Although communicative signals (speech/prosody) contribute to the ratings, the reported contrast isolates temporal coupling with perceived emotional intensity rather than communication per se and does not specifically isolate communicative exchange.
The analysis models participants' ratings of others' emotional intensity and does not isolate self-referential processing at the contrast level.

Moment-to-moment correlation between BOLD and perceived emotional intensity directly indexes representation/inference about others' emotional states (perception_others) in a whole-brain group-level task map of healthy adults.

Negative correlations between BOLD and participants' emotional-intensity ratings are derived from whole-brain task-evoked group analyses in healthy adults and reflect aspects of social/emotional processing (inverse coupling with perceived intensity).
The negative coupling with intensity ratings does not isolate affiliation/attachment-related processing at the contrast level.
The analysis targets momentary inverse coupling with perceived emotional intensity rather than communicative-signal isolation, so it does not meet the social communication inclusion criterion.
The contrast models perception of others' emotional intensity (inverse relationship) and does not isolate self-referential processing.

Negative correlations with participants' continuous ratings still index how neural activity relates to perception/inference about others' emotional states; this is a whole-brain, within-healthy-group measure of perception_others.

The Emotion × Modality interaction is a whole-brain group map in healthy adults that specifically addresses social-emotional processing differences across communicative modalities (facial vs vocal), fulfilling social processing criteria at the contrast level.

Contrast does not isolate self-referential or agency processing (no self-vs-other or explicit self-evaluation contrast).

Contrast does not specifically index representations/inferences about others' mental states; it measures context effects on outcome processing.

FG EX > FG IN is a within-group, whole-brain contrast of social exclusion versus inclusion in the Cyberball task (a canonical social processing paradigm). It directly indexes social processing (ostracism/belonging).
The contrast directly compares exclusion versus inclusion (threat to belonging/attachment), isolating affiliation-related processing at the contrast level.
The contrast does not isolate communicative signal processing (facial/gaze/prosody/gesture/speech); it indexes exclusion/belonging rather than communication.
Although self-related feelings (distress) are relevant, the contrast does not explicitly isolate self-referential or agency processing at the contrast level.
The contrast indexes exclusion versus inclusion but does not explicitly isolate representations/inferences about others' mental states or intentions at the contrast level.

PG EX > FG IN is a whole-brain, within-group task contrast comparing performance-related exclusion to a clean inclusion control; it directly indexes social processing (exclusion with evaluative context).
This contrast contrasts exclusion (with performance evaluation) against inclusion and therefore isolates affiliation/belonging-related processing (threat to social bonds) at the contrast level.
The contrast does not target communicative exchanges or signals; it probes exclusion/evaluation rather than communication per se.
Although authors discuss self-evaluative processes in PG, the reported contrast (PG EX > FG IN) does not explicitly isolate self-referential processing (self vs other) at the contrast level.
While mentalizing regions are reported for PG EX, this contrast does not explicitly isolate representation/inference about others' mental states as the primary measured variable.
The conjunction (PG EX > FG IN ∩ FG EX > FG IN) identifies common exclusion-related activations vs the clean inclusion control; it directly indexes social processing of exclusion/inclusion.
The conjunction isolates regions commonly engaged by exclusion (threat to belonging) compared to inclusion, thus indexing affiliation/attachment-related processing at the contrast level.
The conjunction focuses on exclusion-related processing and does not isolate communicative signal exchange or communication-specific variables.
The conjunction identifies common exclusion activations but does not explicitly isolate self-referential/agency processes at contrast level.
Although some regions related to mentalizing appear in the conjunction, the conjunction itself does not specifically isolate inference about others' mental states as the measured variable.

PG EX > FG EX is a within-group whole-brain contrast comparing two social exclusion contexts (performance-related vs naive); it indexes social processing differences related to evaluative context and exclusion.
This contrast compares two forms of exclusion (performance vs free) and isolates evaluative/stress differences rather than directly isolating affiliation/bonding processes per se.
The contrast differentiates evaluative contexts of exclusion and does not isolate communicative signal processing.

Although authors interpret increased self-evaluative cognition for PG EX, the contrast does not explicitly operationalize self vs other or self-evaluation contrasts; it does not isolate self-processing at contrast level.

PG EX > FG EX shows increased recruitment of mentalizing/ perspective-taking regions (mPFC, precuneus) and authors interpret this as enhanced processing about others (social evaluation/perspective taking), so the contrast indexes perception/understanding of others.

FG EX > PG EX is a within-group whole-brain contrast of social exclusion contexts (free exclusion > performance exclusion); it remains a social processing contrast even if results emphasize visual regions.

This contrast does not isolate affiliation/attachment processes (it compares two exclusion contexts and primarily yields visual-region differences), so it does not meet the affiliation-specific inclusion criterion.
The contrast does not target communicative signal processing and instead reflects context differences of exclusion (visual processing differences reported).
The contrast does not explicitly isolate self-referential or agency processing at the contrast level.

This contrast does not specifically operationalize inference about others' mental states; results emphasized visual cortex rather than mentalizing, so it does not meet the perception-of-others inclusion criterion.

Contrast 'New > Old' indexes relative activation for new items (e.g., visual/novelty-related responses) rather than social processing. Does not meet GLOBAL_I3 (contrast-level requirement) nor SOCIAL_PROCESSING_ALL_I2 (must index social processing at contrast level).
Contrast does not isolate affiliation/attachment-related processing (AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 not met); it reflects novelty/new>old effects.
Contrast does not isolate communication signals or exchanges (SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 not met); it reflects new>old activation patterns (e.g., visual cortex).
The contrast does not explicitly isolate self-related processing (PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 not met); it reflects novelty processing rather than self vs other.
The contrast does not isolate representations/inferences about others (PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1 not met); it indexes new>old effects.
This is an ROI-based analysis in medial PFC (Medial PFC ROI). ROI analyses are excluded by GLOBAL_E1.
Analysis is an ROI and excluded by GLOBAL_E1; additionally, it does not specifically isolate affiliation/attachment at the contrast level (AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 not met).

Whole-brain episodic>control contrasts index engagement of social episodic retrieval mode across tasks (agentic and conceptual self/other recollection). Although the whole-brain analysis indexes social episodic retrieval, it does not specifically isolate affiliation/attachment (e.g., bonding, closeness) at the contrast level (AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 not met).

The whole-brain episodic>control contrast does not isolate communicative signal processing (SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 not met); it indexes general social recollection orientation rather than communication per se.

This contrast collapses across self and other and across old/new, so it does not explicitly isolate self-referential processing (PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 not met). Specific self>other contrasts would be required to satisfy the criterion.

The whole-brain episodic>control contrast does not specifically isolate representations or inferences about others (PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1 not met); it is a general episodic retrieval orientation effect.
